claims.title: Unauthenticated access could let an attacker impersonate a colleague to view shifts
claims.description: `flow:entity:colleague>process:scheduling-web-app>view-shifts` is a decided crossing from the inferred `boundary:public-internet` placement to `boundary:internal-network`, but its `authentication` is unknown. If that attribute resolves to no verified caller identity, an attacker able to initiate the flow can impersonate `entity:colleague` to `process:scheduling-web-app` and obtain the colleague's shift information. This is conditional on the undocumented authentication control, not an assertion that it is absent. Second-order: the web app requests rota data from `process:scheduling-service`, which reads the rota records in `store:rota-database`, so the impersonation reaches the rota information used to answer the request.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high conditional on the unknown authentication value: `flow:entity:colleague>process:scheduling-web-app>view-shifts` is a derived crossing from `boundary:public-internet`, so any internet-originating attacker could attempt the flow if no identity verification is present. Impact is medium because the flow and `entity:colleague` are tagged `pii`, while the stated action is limited to the impersonated colleague's shift response.

mitigations.summary: Establish and enforce colleague authentication on the shift-view flow
mitigations.detail: Document the `authentication` mechanism on `flow:entity:colleague>process:scheduling-web-app>view-shifts` and require a verifiable, user-bound OIDC session or equivalent before `process:scheduling-web-app` serves shift data.

claims.title: Unverified manager identity could let an attacker alter a store rota
claims.description: `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota` crosses from the inferred `boundary:public-internet` placement into `boundary:internal-network`, while its `authentication` is unknown. If no verified identity and session binding are actually enforced, an attacker can impersonate `entity:store-manager` to `process:scheduling-web-app` and submit rota changes as that manager. This is conditional on the unknown authentication attribute. Second-order: the app sends rota reads and writes to `process:scheduling-service`, which writes rota and colleague-detail records in `store:rota-database`; the spoofed manager identity therefore reaches business-critical scheduling data rather than only the web tier.

quotes.text: Store managers use a scheduling web app to build the weekly rota for their store.
The scheduling service is what actually reads and writes the rotas

severity.justification: Likelihood is high conditional on the unknown authentication value: `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota` is a derived crossing from `boundary:public-internet`, permitting broad attacker access if identity verification is absent. Impact is high because the flow carries `pii` and `business-critical-data` and the impersonated manager can cause writes through `process:scheduling-service` to `store:rota-database`, which has the same asset tags.

mitigations.summary: Require verified, user-bound manager authentication
mitigations.detail: Set an explicit authentication control on `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota`, such as OIDC with phishing-resistant MFA for manager accounts, and bind rota-changing sessions to the verified manager identity.

mitigations.summary: Constrain rota writes to the authenticated manager's store
mitigations.detail: Have `process:scheduling-web-app` and `process:scheduling-service` derive the manager and store scope from the verified identity rather than from caller-controlled rota data.

claims.title: Unverified payroll-system identity could expose the weekly payroll export
claims.description: `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export` is a decided crossing from the payroll team's inferred trust-zone placement into `boundary:internal-network`, but its `authentication` is unknown. If the file share does not verify the caller, an attacker with access to the payroll-system side of that path can impersonate `entity:payroll-system` to `store:file-share` and collect the weekly payroll export. This is conditional on the undocumented authentication control; it does not assert that the share is unauthenticated. The exported data is tagged `pii`, so the successful impersonation exposes payroll information beyond the purported external collector.

quotes.text: The payroll system, which is run by another team, collects the export from the file share.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium conditional on the unknown authentication value: the flow crosses into the internal network, but exploitation requires an attacker to reach the payroll-system side of that path rather than merely connect from the public internet. Impact is medium because `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export` and `store:file-share` are tagged `pii`, and the action retrieves the weekly payroll export.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate the payroll collector with a unique workload identity
mitigations.detail: Document and enforce mutual TLS or short-lived workload-federated credentials on `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export`; authorize that identity only to read its intended export.

mitigations.summary: Protect payroll-export retrieval against replay
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived, audience-bound access tokens or mTLS identities rather than a reusable shared credential, and record the authenticated collector identity for each export retrieval.

claims.title: Unauthorized rota changes if manager authentication and authorization are unverified
claims.description: If the unverified `authentication` on `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota` does not enforce a manager identity and store-level authorization, an attacker reaching the web app from the manager-side boundary can submit altered rota entries through `process:scheduling-web-app`. The flow is a decided crossing from `boundary:public-internet` to `boundary:internal-network`, although both endpoint placements were inferred by the model. Second-order, `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests` carries rota writes to `process:scheduling-service`, which writes the altered rota into `store:rota-database`; colleagues subsequently receive incorrect shift information through the app.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication control: the manager write flow crosses from `boundary:public-internet` into the internal network, but the model does not establish whether an attacker can authenticate or bypass authorization. Impact is high because altered rota entries become authoritative in `store:rota-database`, which holds `business-critical-data` and colleague PII, affecting scheduling for the store.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and authorize rota changes
mitigations.detail: Define and enforce authentication on `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota`, and have `process:scheduling-web-app` verify server-side that the authenticated manager may modify only their own store's rota.

mitigations.summary: Validate rota mutations before persistence
mitigations.detail: Have `process:scheduling-service` enforce allowlisted rota fields, store ownership checks, and change validation before writing to `store:rota-database`.

claims.title: Direct modification of rota records if database write authentication is unverified
claims.description: If `authentication` on `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:rota-database>read-write-rotas` permits an untrusted or overly broad caller, an attacker with an internal-network foothold can alter rota entries, colleague contact details, or stated availability directly in `store:rota-database`, bypassing the scheduling service's normal request path. The store is the authoritative source: `process:scheduling-service` initiates the read-write flow to consume these records, then serves rota reads and writes through `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests`; corrupted records therefore propagate to the web app and its users as legitimate scheduling data. This is conditional on the currently unverified database-flow authentication, not an assertion that the store accepts unauthenticated writes.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown authentication value because the attacker needs an internal-network foothold or a caller identity accepted by the store. Impact is high because `store:rota-database` contains rota data tagged `business-critical-data` plus colleague PII, and `process:scheduling-service` consumes the altered records as authoritative.

mitigations.summary: Use a dedicated least-privilege database identity
mitigations.detail: Authenticate `process:scheduling-service` to `store:rota-database` with a workload-specific identity and grant only the required read and write operations rather than broad direct database access.

mitigations.summary: Restrict and verify database write paths
mitigations.detail: Apply deny-by-default store access policies and ensure rota ownership and mutation rules are enforced by `process:scheduling-service` or database-side controls before records can be changed.

claims.title: Payroll export can be altered before collection if file-share writes are not authenticated
claims.description: If the unverified `authentication` on `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:file-share>write-payroll-export` allows an untrusted or insufficiently constrained writer, an attacker with access accepted by the file share can alter the weekly payroll export in `store:file-share` after it is written. The attacker changes payroll data at rest rather than merely intercepting its collection. Second-order, `entity:payroll-system` consumes the export through `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export` and may treat the altered file as the scheduling service's genuine weekly payroll input. This is conditional on the unknown write authentication and authorization model.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown authentication control because exploitation requires access accepted by the internal file-share write path. Impact is medium because the altered asset is the weekly payroll export carrying PII and is subsequently collected by `entity:payroll-system`, potentially causing incorrect payroll processing.

mitigations.summary: Enforce authenticated, least-privilege export writes
mitigations.detail: Give only `process:scheduling-service` a dedicated write identity for the payroll-export location in `store:file-share`, and restrict other principals to the minimum required read access.

mitigations.summary: Sign and verify payroll exports
mitigations.detail: Have `process:scheduling-service` sign each versioned export and require `entity:payroll-system` to verify its signature and expected metadata before processing it.

claims.title: A manager may be able to deny making a rota change
claims.description: `entity:store-manager` changes rota entries through `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota`, then through `process:scheduling-web-app` and `process:scheduling-service` to `store:rota-database`. The manager-facing boundary crossing and the authentication on that flow are documented only as unknown; authentication is also unknown on `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests` and `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:rota-database>read-write-rotas`. If these unknowns do not resolve to an individually authenticated identity that is propagated and retained in an audit record, a manager who alters a business-critical rota can plausibly deny doing so because the system cannot bind the database change to them. The model also contains no `audit log` element, so it does not show an independent record of who changed a rota, when, or with what outcome. Second-order, disputed rota changes can affect schedules and the weekly payroll export produced by `process:scheduling-service`, while leaving the operator unable to distinguish an error, fraud, or a legitimate correction.

quotes.text: Nobody has documented how colleagues or managers sign in, how the web app and the scheduling service identify each other

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication controls on the manager boundary crossing and both internal write-path flows: a manager already able to use the scheduling app can dispute a normal rota change, but the undocumented controls may provide individual attribution. Impact is medium because `store:rota-database` holds `business-critical-data` and PII, and disputed changes can propagate into payroll-export processing.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate each manager individually and preserve the verified subject
mitigations.detail: Use individual, non-shared authentication on `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota`, and propagate the verified subject through `process:scheduling-web-app` and `process:scheduling-service` rather than replacing it with a service identity.

mitigations.summary: Create an independent rota-change audit trail
mitigations.detail: Emit structured records for rota writes with the verified actor, action, affected rota entry, before/after values, timestamp, request identifier, and outcome. Send them to dedicated append-only audit storage under a separate write principal and retention lock.

claims.title: Unverified public-app transport may expose colleague shifts and store rotas
claims.description: The derived boundary-crossing flows `flow:entity:colleague>process:scheduling-web-app>view-shifts` and `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota` carry PII, and the latter carries store rota data, but both have `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If transport protection is absent or incorrectly terminated, an on-path attacker on a colleague's phone network or the public-to-app route can intercept colleagues' shifts and managers' store rota entries. The boundary placement for the app is inferred in the model, so this is conditional on both the derived path and the unresolved transport control. The disclosed schedules and identities enable targeted attacks against colleagues and better-targeted requests to `process:scheduling-web-app`.

quotes.text: Colleagues reach the app from their own phones.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because both public-facing flows cross a trust boundary but their `encryption_in_transit` attributes are unknown, while observation still requires an on-path position. Impact is medium because the flows carry `pii`, and the manager flow additionally carries store rota entries and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce TLS for both public app interactions
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` to TLS 1.2+ or stronger on both public-to-`process:scheduling-web-app` flows, validate certificates on clients, and document where TLS terminates.

mitigations.summary: Minimize data returned to clients
mitigations.detail: Return only the fields needed for a colleague's own shifts and the manager's current rota operation, avoiding unnecessary personal fields in responses.

claims.title: Unverified internal transport may expose rota records and payroll exports
claims.description: `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests`, `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:rota-database>read-write-rotas`, and `flow:process:scheduling-service>store:file-share>write-payroll-export` all carry PII or business-critical rota and payroll data, yet each has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If any internal hop is plaintext, an attacker with a foothold capable of observing that segment can intercept rota requests, colleague contact details and availability, or the weekly payroll export. The internal network is not itself evidence of transport confidentiality. The resulting records enable targeted attacks on colleagues and provide context for attacks against the scheduling and payroll workflows.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the three unknown transport-control values: exploitation requires an internal on-path foothold, but no stated encryption reduces that prerequisite to gaining such visibility. Impact is medium because these flows carry `pii`, rota data, and the payroll export, exposing more than a single user interaction.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate all service and storage hops
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ for the web-app-to-service, service-to-database, and service-to-file-share flows; use mTLS for service peers and validate the protected endpoint on every connection.

mitigations.summary: Document and test internal transport posture
mitigations.detail: Record the protocol and `encryption_in_transit` setting for every internal flow, including database and file-share client configurations, and reject plaintext connections.

claims.title: Payroll export may be readable while collected across an unverified external path
claims.description: `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export` crosses from `boundary:payroll-team-environment` to the internal file share and carries the weekly payroll export, but its `encryption_in_transit` setting is unknown. If that collection channel is not encrypted, an attacker able to observe the path between the other team's payroll system and `store:file-share` can intercept the export. The disclosure gives the attacker information about the payroll workflow and employees that can support targeted attacks against the separately operated `entity:payroll-system`.

quotes.text: The payroll system, which is run by another team, collects the export from the file share.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses into an environment run by another team while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown; an attacker must obtain an on-path position. Impact is medium because `store:file-share` and the collection flow carry `pii` in a recurring payroll export.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated encrypted payroll-export collection
mitigations.detail: Use TLS 1.2+ for `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export`, preferably with mutually authenticated workload identities for the payroll system and file share.

mitigations.summary: Use protected, short-lived export delivery
mitigations.detail: Expose each export through a short-lived, access-controlled download or transfer mechanism rather than a broadly reachable share path.

claims.title: An unverified payroll-collection identity may expose the file-share export
claims.description: The external `entity:payroll-system` initiates the read flow `flow:entity:payroll-system>store:file-share>collect-payroll-export`, but that flow's `authentication` is unknown. If the file share does not strongly authenticate and authorize the payroll collector, an unauthorized party able to reach the collection interface can read the PII-bearing weekly export from `store:file-share`. This is conditional on the undocumented authentication state, not an assertion that access is unauthenticated. A copied export enables targeting of people represented in the payroll workflow and can be reused wherever the same personnel information is trusted.

quotes.text: Nobody has documented ... how the payroll system is identified when it collects the export

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because an external system reads from the file share and the flow's authentication is unknown, although an attacker must reach that interface. Impact is medium because the file share and collection flow are tagged `pii` and expose a complete weekly payroll export rather than one colleague interaction.

mitigations.summary: Enforce a dedicated payroll-reader identity
mitigations.detail: Require a distinct, strongly authenticated service identity for `entity:payroll-system` and authorize it only to read the required export objects.

mitigations.summary: Constrain export access and retention
mitigations.detail: Use per-export access controls, short-lived grants, and an auditable retrieval record so a reader cannot enumerate historical payroll exports.

claims.title: Rota database copies may disclose colleague data if storage encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:rota-database` holds rota entries, colleague names, contact details, and availability, is tagged `pii`, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains an operational copy of the database media, such as a storage-layer snapshot or decommissioned volume, can read its contents without using `process:scheduling-service` or its normal database flow. This is conditional on the unresolved at-rest control; it does not claim the database is currently unencrypted. The data reveals when and how to target colleagues and provides the personal context used by the scheduling workflow.

quotes.text: Colleague names, contact details and stated availability are held in that database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` value: a storage-layer copy must be obtained, but no stated encryption protects it. Impact is medium because `store:rota-database` holds colleague PII including contact details and availability, making disclosure irreversible and useful for targeted abuse.

mitigations.summary: Establish and enforce encryption at rest for rota data
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:rota-database`'s at-rest posture, then use managed envelope encryption with controlled key access for the primary data and every operational copy.

mitigations.summary: Restrict and audit storage-copy access
mitigations.detail: Limit creation, export, and restoration of database snapshots or other storage copies to dedicated principals, and monitor those actions.

claims.title: File-share copies may disclose payroll exports if storage encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:file-share` holds the PII-bearing weekly payroll export and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If the share or its operational copies are not encrypted at rest, an attacker who gains storage-layer access can read exported payroll data directly without authenticating as `entity:payroll-system`. This is a conditional finding about the unresolved attribute, not a claim that encryption is absent. The copied export can then be used to target people and workflows associated with the payroll collection path.

quotes.text: Once a week the scheduling service writes a payroll export onto a file share.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:file-share` has no verified at-rest encryption, though an attacker must obtain storage-layer access or a copy. Impact is medium because the share contains a recurring payroll export tagged `pii`, and disclosure cannot be recalled once copied.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the file share and all operational copies
mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce encryption at rest on `store:file-share`, including snapshots, backups, and replicas, with keys unavailable to ordinary share readers.

mitigations.summary: Limit payroll-export lifetime
mitigations.detail: Delete or archive exports under a defined retention policy after the payroll system has collected them, reducing the amount of PII available in the share.

claims.title: Flooding the shared scheduling web app can deny rota access to managers and colleagues
claims.description: An attacker starting from the public-internet side can send a high volume of requests over `flow:entity:colleague>process:scheduling-web-app>view-shifts` and `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota` to exhaust finite request-handling capacity in `process:scheduling-web-app`. Authentication on both boundary-crossing flows is `unknown`, so this is conditional on those paths permitting unauthenticated or insufficiently metered requests; the model does not establish that the app rejects excessive work before it reaches the scheduling path. The attacker spends cheap repeated requests while the app must accept, route, and handle each interaction. Second-order, saturation prevents both colleagues from viewing shifts and managers from maintaining rotas, and traffic propagated over `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests` can also delay the service's rota reads and writes.

quotes.text: The web app talks to a scheduling service.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional: both attacker-facing flows cross from `boundary:public-internet`, but their `authentication` attributes are unknown and the boundary endpoint placements were inferred. Impact is medium because `process:scheduling-web-app` is the shared entry point for both shift viewing and weekly rota changes, and its downstream `process:scheduling-service` performs the rota reads and writes; the resulting interruption is operationally significant but recoverable.

mitigations.summary: Apply request and concurrency limits at the scheduling web app
mitigations.detail: Set per-verified-user and per-source rate limits, bounded concurrent requests, and load shedding on `process:scheduling-web-app` before requests are forwarded over `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests`.

mitigations.summary: Establish and enforce the boundary authentication posture
mitigations.detail: Document the authentication mechanism for both public-to-app flows and require authenticated identity before expensive rota operations, with separate quotas for colleague shift reads and manager rota changes.

mitigations.summary: Bound downstream work and failure propagation
mitigations.detail: Use timeouts, bounded queues, and circuit breaking between `process:scheduling-web-app` and `process:scheduling-service` so an inbound flood cannot indefinitely consume service capacity.

claims.title: Scheduling web app may let a colleague gain rota-management authority
claims.description: `process:scheduling-web-app` is the common enforcement point for `flow:entity:colleague>process:scheduling-web-app>view-shifts`, intended for a colleague's own shifts, and `flow:entity:store-manager>process:scheduling-web-app>build-rota`, which changes rota entries for a store. Both flows cross from `boundary:public-internet` into `boundary:internal-network`, while authentication is undocumented. If `process:scheduling-web-app` does not independently authenticate the caller and enforce the manager role on every write route, a colleague using their legitimate app access could invoke the rota-management path and gain authority to alter the store rota. The resulting writes travel through `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests` to `process:scheduling-service`, which reads and writes `store:rota-database`; this can alter rota records and the associated colleague information. This is conditional on the unstated server-side authentication and role authorization, not an assertion that those controls are absent.

quotes.text: Nobody has documented how colleagues or managers sign in

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional: `flow:entity:colleague>process:scheduling-web-app>view-shifts` is a crossing from the public-internet zone, but authentication on both colleague and manager flows is unknown and server-side role enforcement is unstated. Impact is high because manager-level writes reach `process:scheduling-service`, which reads and writes `store:rota-database`, an element tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Enforce server-side manager authorization on every rota write
mitigations.detail: Have `process:scheduling-web-app` authenticate the caller and apply centralized, deny-by-default authorization middleware to every route that creates or changes rota entries; never rely on a client-side role flag or hidden route.

mitigations.summary: Bind rota changes to the manager's authorized store
mitigations.detail: Derive the manager's permitted store scope from the verified identity and enforce it before forwarding each write on `flow:process:scheduling-web-app>process:scheduling-service>rota-requests`.
